mainTopic: Rewards of שבת and the sages' cherished practices (שבת קיח:)
overview: The amud begins by finishing the rewards for עונג שבת: a boundless inheritance like יעקב's, rescue from exile, and the granting of one's heart's desires. The גמרא explains that עונג שבת can be a fine meal or even a small dish, as long as it is made לכבוד שבת. רבי יוחנן teaches that keeping שבת properly brings forgiveness even for idolatry like דור אנוש. Two statements tie the fate of ישראל to שבת: breaking the first שבת brought עמלק, and keeping two שבתות would bring immediate גאולה. Then comes a long list of רבי יוסי's 'יהא חלקי' wishes, such as שלש סעודות, daily פסוקי דזמרא, and davening at sunrise and sunset. Each one is clarified when the גמרא raises a question. Next come רבי יוסי's personal statements about his five sons, his refined speech, his modesty, and his honesty. Finally, several אמוראים name the מצוה each was especially careful with, using the phrase 'תיתי לי'. A story shows רבה's care for ציצית, and אביי begins a statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the reward is the inheritance of יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the verse 'נחלת יעקב אביך' and explains that יעקב's portion has no borders, unlike the portions promised to אברהם and יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...the inheritance of יעקב your father.' Not like אברהם, about whom it says 'Rise, walk the land along its length.' And not like יצחק, about whom it says 'To you and your children I will give all these lands.' Rather like יעקב, about whom it says 'You will spread out west, east, north and south.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing the statement (begun on the previous amud) that one who delights in שבת receives a 'נחלה בלי מצרים', an inheritance without borders. Here it explains why the verse says 'יעקב' specifically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם was shown one specific land, and יצחק was promised 'these lands', so both had limits. Only יעקב was told he would spread out in all four directions with no limit. So 'the inheritance of יעקב' means a reward without borders.

keyTerms.meaning: The inheritance of יעקב, a portion without borders
Along its length, which implies a measured, limited land
And you will burst out, spreading with no limit

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The verse began on the previous page, where the reward of 'נחלה בלי מצרים' (an inheritance without borders) was stated. This step only explains the last words of that verse.

phrases.english: "...the inheritance of Yaakov your father, etc."
phrases.notes: End of ישעיה נח:יד, quoted on the previous page

phrases.english: Not like Avraham, about whom it is written:
"Rise, walk through the land along its length, etc."
And not like Yitzchak, about whom it is written:
"For to you and to your offspring I will give
all these lands."
phrases.notes: 'These' lands, meaning specific ones and no others

phrases.english: Rather, like Yaakov, about whom it is written:
"And you will spread out to the west, east, north and south."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the verse and the reasoning of the statement that began on the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reward for עונג שבת is a boundless inheritance, like the one promised to יעקב.

steps.title: Another reward: rescue from exile
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the same verse differently. The reward is being saved from the oppression of exile, learned from a word-link on 'heights'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: He is saved from the oppression of the exiles. It is written here, 'I will make you ride on the heights of the earth,' and it is written there, 'And you will trample on their heights.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different reward for עונג שבת: being saved from שעבוד גליות, the domination of the nations in exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He links the word 'במתי' in the שבת verse to 'במותימו' in דברים, which speaks of יִשְׂרָאֵל trampling its enemies. Since the same word appears in both, the שבת verse is also promising victory over the oppressing nations.

keyTerms.meaning: Oppression or subjugation of the exiles
It is written here... and it is written there, the standard wording of a גזירה שוה

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
He is rescued from the oppression of exile.
It is written here: "I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth,"
phrases.notes: ישעיה נח:יד, in the שבת passage

phrases.english: and it is written there:
"And you will trample upon their high places."
phrases.notes: דברים לג:כט, about victory over enemies

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reward based on the same verse
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who delights in שבת is saved from the domination of the nations in exile.

steps.title: Delighting in שבת brings one's heart's desires
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that whoever delights in שבת is granted his heart's desires, based on a verse in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Whoever delights in שבת is given his heart's desires, as it says: 'Delight in ה׳ and He will give you the desires of your heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement from רב יהודה in the name of רב: the reward for עונג שבת is getting what your heart asks for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof verse says 'והתענג על ה׳', delight in ה׳, and does not mention שבת. So the גמרא will immediately need to show why this verse is about שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes שבת a delight
The requests or desires of his heart

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Anyone who delights in Shabbat
is given his heart's desires,
as it is stated: "Delight in ה׳
and He will give you the desires of your heart."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another reward for עונג שבת, from a new source
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who delights in שבת receives his heart's desires.

steps.title: Which delight does the verse mean?
steps.stepSummary: The verse in תהלים says 'delight' but does not say which delight. The question is what kind of delight is meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: This 'delight' — I do not know what it is.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks how we know that the 'delight' in the verse refers to שבת, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this question, רב's proof would have a gap, because the verse never mentions שבת. The question shows that the link has to be proven.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know what it is

phrases.english: This delight, I do not know what it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the proof verse in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of 'delight' does the verse in תהלים mean?

steps.title: The delight is the delight of שבת
steps.stepSummary: Since ישעיה calls שבת 'עונג', the delight mentioned in תהלים must be עונג שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'And you shall call שבת a delight,' we must say this is the delight of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a verse that calls שבת itself 'עונג'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עונג' is attached to שבת in ישעיה. So when 'delight' appears elsewhere without explanation, we read it as the delight of שבת. This closes the gap in רב's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall call שבת a delight (ישעיה נח:יג)
You must say, it must be

phrases.english: When it says "And you shall call Shabbat a delight" —
you must say: this is the delight of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'delight' in תהלים is עונג שבת, because ישעיה calls שבת 'עונג'.

steps.title: How does one delight in שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical meaning: with what does a person make שבת a delight?
steps.simpleTranslation: With what does one delight in it?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. Now that we know the reward, the גמרא asks what a person should actually do to make שבת a delight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion moves from the reward to the practice. The answers that follow describe specific foods.

keyTerms.meaning: With what does one delight it?

phrases.english: With what does one delight in it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical definition of עונג שבת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What concrete actions or foods count as delighting in שבת?

steps.title: Beets, big fish, and garlic
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רב: one delights in שבת with a dish of beets, large fish, and heads of garlic.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בריה דרב שמואל בר שילת said in the name of רב: With a dish of beets, large fish, and heads of garlic.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer lists specific foods that make שבת a delight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These were considered fine, enjoyable foods in their time. The answer suggests that עונג שבת involves a real, festive meal.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat,
said in the name of Rav:
With a dish of beets,
and large fish, and heads of garlic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With beets, large fish, and garlic.

steps.title: Even a small dish counts if made for שבת
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching of רב: even a small, simple item counts as עונג if it was prepared in honor of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: Even a small thing, if one made it in honor of שבת, is a delight.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer widens the definition. It is not only about expensive food. Even a little thing counts if it was made for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is the intention, 'לכבוד שבת'. The size or cost of the dish is not what matters. This makes עונג שבת possible even for someone who cannot afford a lavish meal.
steps.whyThisMatters: Halachically, this teaches that the purpose 'לכבוד שבת' is what turns ordinary food into a fulfillment of עונג שבת.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
Even a small item,
if one prepared it in honor of Shabbat —
this is a delight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ דָּבָר מוּעָט, וְלִכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת עֲשָׂאוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, broader answer to step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even a small item prepared in honor of שבת counts as עונג.

steps.title: What is the 'small item'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for an example of the 'small item' just mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא wants a concrete example of the 'דבר מועט'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'a small item' is vague, so the גמרא asks for a specific example.

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of 'דבר מועט' in step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is an example of the small item?

steps.title: A dish of small fried fish
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the small item is כסא דהרסנא, a dish of small fish fried in flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: A dish of small fried fish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the example: a simple, cheap dish of small fried fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This was an inexpensive, everyday food. Yet when prepared for שבת, it counts as עונג שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A dish of small fish fried in flour or oil

steps.whatToRemember: עונג שבת can be a festive meal (beets, large fish, garlic) or even a small, simple dish, as long as it is made לכבוד שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: A dish of small fried fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The small item is a dish of small fried fish.

steps.title: Keeping שבת properly brings forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that whoever keeps שבת properly is forgiven even for עבודה זרה like that of דור אנוש. He reads 'מחללו' as 'מחול לו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Whoever keeps שבת according to its laws, even if he worships idols like דור אנוש, is forgiven. As it says: 'Fortunate is the man (אנוש) who does this... from desecrating it (מחללו).' Do not read 'מחללו' but 'מחול לו' (he is forgiven).
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching moves from delighting in שבת to keeping it properly. Doing so earns forgiveness even for very severe sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אנוש' in the verse hints at דור אנוש, the generation that began idol worship. Using an 'אל תקרי' reading, 'מחללו' (desecrating it) is read as 'מחול לו' (he is forgiven). Together, the verse says that even someone who sinned like דור אנוש is forgiven if he keeps שבת properly.

keyTerms.meaning: One who keeps שבת according to its laws
The generation of אנוש, who began idol worship
Do not read it as... but as, a דרש re-reading

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not change the actual text of the פסוק. It is a דרש that adds a second layer of meaning on top of the plain reading.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who keeps Shabbat according to its laws,
even if he worships idols like the generation of Enosh —
he is forgiven,
as it is stated: "Fortunate is the man (enosh) who does this
etc. ...from desecrating it."
Do not read "from desecrating it (mechalelo)"
but rather: "he is forgiven (machul lo)."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from rewards of עונג שבת to the reward for שמירת שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keeping שבת properly brings forgiveness, even for sins as grave as the idolatry of דור אנוש.

steps.title: Had ישראל kept the first שבת, no nation would rule them
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that because some of יִשְׂרָאֵל broke the very first שבת (going out to collect מן), עמלק came, and nations gained power over them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Had ישראל kept the first שבת, no nation or tongue would have ruled over them. As it says: 'On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather,' and right after it is written: 'And עמלק came.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב connects the failure to keep the first שבת in the מדבר with the attack of עמלק right afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is from the order of the פסוקים. Right after people went out to gather מן on שבת, the תורה tells of עמלק's attack. רב reads this order as cause and effect: breaking שבת opened the door to foreign domination.

keyTerms.meaning: The first שבת commanded in the מדבר
Nation and tongue, meaning any foreign people
And it is written after it

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Had Israel kept the first Shabbat,
no nation or tongue would have ruled over them,
as it is stated: "And it was on the seventh day,
some of the people went out to gather,"
and it is written after it: "And Amalek came."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the power of שמירת שבת, now on the national level
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Failure to keep the first שבת led to foreign nations ruling over יִשְׂרָאֵל.

steps.title: Keeping two שבתות properly would bring immediate redemption
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches that if יִשְׂרָאֵל kept two שבתות properly, they would be redeemed immediately, based on the order of verses in ישעיה נו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: If ישראל would keep two שבתות according to their laws, they would be redeemed immediately. As it says: 'So says ה׳ to the eunuchs who keep My שבתות,' and after it is written: 'And I will bring them to My holy mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The positive side of the previous step: keeping שבת properly, twice, would bring the גאולה at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שבתותי' is plural, and the minimum plural is two, so two שבתות are meant. The very next promise in the passage is being brought to 'My holy mountain', which means redemption. Again the proof rests on the order of the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: My holy mountain, the place of redemption

steps.whatToRemember: This pair of statements gives a national message: breaking the first שבת brought enemies like עמלק, while keeping two שבתות properly would bring immediate גאולה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
If only Israel would keep
two Shabbatot according to their laws —
they would be redeemed immediately,
as it is stated: "So says ה׳ to the eunuchs
who will keep My Shabbatot,"
phrases.notes: ישעיה נו:ד, plural, meaning at least two

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב בָּתְרֵיהּ: ״וַהֲבִיאוֹתִים אֶל הַר קׇדְשִׁי וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and it is written after it: "And I will bring them to My holy mountain, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִלְמָלֵי מְשַׁמְּרִין יִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת כְּהִלְכָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The positive counterpart to step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keeping two שבתות properly would bring immediate redemption.

steps.title: Wishing to be among those who eat three meals on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי wishes to share the reward of those who eat three meals on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: May my share be with those who eat three meals on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי praises eating three meals on שבת by saying he wants his reward to be with the people who do this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the earlier theme of honoring שבת, which included rewards for enjoying שבת and keeping it properly. Saying 'May my portion be with them' shows that eating שלש סעודות is an act worth a great reward. It also opens a chain of other 'יהא חלקי' statements from רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be
among those who eat three meals on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of praises for keeping and honoring שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating three meals on שבת deserves a share of reward that רבי יוסי himself wishes for.

steps.title: Wishing to be among those who complete הלל every day
steps.stepSummary: Following the first wish, the גמרא brings another one: רבי יוסי wishes to be among those who finish הלל every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: May my share be with those who complete הלל every day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a list of other wishes from רבי יוסי. This one is about saying הלל every day, and it sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic is no longer שבת. The גמרא is now collecting all of רבי יוסי's 'יהא חלקי' statements together. On its face, this wish sounds like a daily recital of the special הלל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be
among those who complete hallel every day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: יְהֵא חֶלְקִי מִגּוֹמְרֵי הַלֵּל בְּכׇל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same speaker and formula, but a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי praises completing הלל every day.

steps.title: Challenge: reading הלל daily is disrespectful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוסי could praise saying הלל daily, since a known teaching calls this like cursing and blaspheming.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? Didn't the Master say: Whoever reads הלל every day is like someone who curses and blasphemes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's wish by quoting a teaching that saying הלל every day is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל was set aside for special days when miracles happened. Reciting it every day turns it into a routine song, which shows contempt for it. So praising a daily הלל seems to clash with this teaching.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not say הלל is bad. It says that turning the special holiday הלל into a daily routine is disrespectful.

phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't the Master say:
One who reads hallel every day
is like one who curses and blasphemes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wish in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's praise of completing הלל every day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known teaching says saying הלל daily is disrespectful, so it cannot be something to wish for.

steps.title: Answer: he meant פסוקי דזמרא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי's 'הלל' means פסוקי דזמרא, the daily morning praises, not the holiday הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we say this, we mean פסוקי דזמרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what kind of 'הלל' רבי יוסי meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of praise. The holiday הלל (תהלים קיג–קיח) should not be said daily, but פסוקי דזמרא are daily praises in the morning davening. רבי יוסי praised finishing those every day, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: When we said it, we meant…
Verses of praise said daily in שחרית

steps.whatToRemember: The holiday הלל is not said every day. פסוקי דזמרא are the daily praises, and completing them is praiseworthy.

phrases.english: When we say this, it refers to the verses of praise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term: 'הלל' refers to פסוקי דזמרא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי meant the holiday הלל, which would be disrespectful to say daily.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant פסוקי דזמרא, which are meant to be said daily.

steps.title: Wishing to pray at sunrise and sunset
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי wishes to be among those who daven with דמדומי חמה, the reddening of the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: May my share be with those who daven when the sun is red.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives another wish: to daven at the time the sun turns red.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דמדומי חמה means the sun's reddish glow. For שחרית this is sunrise, and for מנחה it is near sunset. The ideal is to daven at these exact edge times.

keyTerms.meaning: The reddening of the sun (sunrise or sunset)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be
among those who pray with the reddening of the sun.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: יְהֵא חֶלְקִי מִמִּתְפַּלְּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another item in רבי יוסי's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Davening at sunrise and sunset is praiseworthy.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: it is a מצוה to pray at the sun's reddening
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoted by רבי חייא בר אבא, says davening at the sun's reddening is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is a מצוה to daven when the sun is red.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds an אמורא who supports רבי יוסי's wish and calls it a real מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי only said he wished for this. רבי יוחנן goes further and says it is a מצוה. This raises it from a personal wish to a recommended practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A commandment or recommended good deed

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the practice of davening שחרית at sunrise (ותיקין).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is a מצוה to pray with the reddening of the sun.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 18 and makes it stronger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Davening with דמדומי חמה is a מצוה.

steps.title: רבי זירא gives the verse for praying with the sun
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא brings a פסוק from תהלים as the source for davening at sunrise and sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: What is the source? 'They will fear You with the sun, and before the moon, for all generations.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks which פסוק hints at this, then answers with a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Fearing You' means davening. 'With the sun' means davening as the sun rises, and 'before the moon' means davening before night comes. So the פסוק hints at both the morning and afternoon times.

keyTerms.meaning: They will fear You with the sun

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: What is the verse?
"They will fear You with the sun
and before the moon, generation upon generation."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural source for רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.raayaObject: The מצוה to daven with דמדומי חמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים עב:ה — יִירָאוּךָ עִם שָׁמֶשׁ וְלִפְנֵי יָרֵחַ

steps.title: Wishing to die of intestinal illness, like most righteous people
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי wishes to die from a stomach illness, because most צדיקים die that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: May my share be with those who die from stomach illness, because the Master said most צדיקים die from stomach illness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a surprising wish, and the גמרא explains it with a known teaching about צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This illness is painful, and the suffering wipes away a person's sins before death. That is why it is common among צדיקים, and why רבי יוסי wanted to share their end.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be
among those who die of intestinal disease,
as the Master said:
Most righteous people
die of intestinal disease.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: יְהֵא חֶלְקִי מִמֵּתֵי בְּחוֹלִי מֵעַיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another item in רבי יוסי's list, this time with a reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dying of stomach illness is the way most צדיקים die, so it is desirable.

steps.title: Wishing to die while on the way to a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי wishes to die while going to do a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: May my share be with those who die on the way to do a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: Another wish from רבי יוסי: to die in the middle of doing something holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dying while busy with a מצוה means leaving the world in a moment of serving God. It is a mark of an honorable end.

keyTerms.meaning: On the way to a מצוה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be
among those who die on the path to a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: יְהֵא חֶלְקִי מִמֵּתֵי בְּדֶרֶךְ מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second wish about a good kind of death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dying on the way to a מצוה is a worthy end.

steps.title: Wishing to start שבת early in טבריה and end it late in ציפורי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי wishes to bring in שבת early like the people of טבריה and end it late like the people of ציפורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: May my share be with those who start שבת in טבריה and end שבת in ציפורי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי praises making שבת longer at both ends by naming two towns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבריה is in a valley, so the sun disappears early and שבת starts early. ציפורי is on a mountain, so the sun is seen longer and שבת ends late. Together they show adding time to שבת on both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: טבריה, a town in a low valley
ציפורי, a town on a mountain

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be
among those who usher in Shabbat in Tiberias,
and among those who see Shabbat out in Tzippori.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: יְהֵא חֶלְקִי מִמַּכְנִיסֵי שַׁבָּת בִּטְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another item in the list, this one returning to שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is praiseworthy to start שבת early and end it late.

steps.title: Wishing to seat people in the study hall, not send them out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי wishes to be among those who bring people in to sit and learn, not those who tell them to get up and leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: May my share be with those who seat people in the בית המדרש, and not with those who make them stand up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי contrasts two roles in the בית המדרש and picks the one that brings people to learn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Seating' means getting people to come in and learn. 'Making them stand' means announcing that it is time to stop and go eat. רבי יוסי would rather be the cause of more learning, not the one who ends it.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who seat people in the study hall
Those who make people stand up and leave the study hall

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be
among those who seat others in the study hall,
and not among those who make others stand in the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: יְהֵא חֶלְקִי מִמּוֹשִׁיבֵי בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another item in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is better to bring people into learning than to send them out.

steps.title: Wishing to collect charity rather than distribute it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי prefers being a צדקה collector over a צדקה distributor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: May my share be with those who collect צדקה, and not with those who hand it out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי compares two charity jobs and picks the one with less risk of doing wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collectors take set amounts, so it is clear what is right. Distributors must judge each poor person's needs and may accidentally give too little. רבי יוסי preferred the job with less risk of letting a poor person down.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be
among the collectors of charity
and not the distributors of charity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: יְהֵא חֶלְקִי מִגַּבַּאי צְדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another item in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Collecting צדקה is preferable to distributing it, since distributing carries more risk of error.

steps.title: Wishing to be falsely suspected
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי wishes to be among those who are suspected of sin but are innocent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: May my share be with someone people suspect, but who did nothing wrong.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives his last 'יהא חלקי' wish: to be someone who is wrongly suspected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being falsely suspected is painful and unfair. Bearing it while being truly innocent earns great reward, which is why רבי יוסי wished for it.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is not in him (he is innocent)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be
with one whom others suspect
and there is no basis for it in him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: יְהֵא חֶלְקִי מִמִּי שֶׁחוֹשְׁדִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another item in the list; it sets up רב פפא's comment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An innocent person who is falsely suspected has a portion worth wishing for.

steps.title: רב פפא: I was falsely suspected
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says he himself was suspected of something and was innocent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: They suspected me, and it was not true of me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a personal note showing that רבי יוסי's last wish came true for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא is saying he has the portion רבי יוסי wished for. It closes the list with a real-life example.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's list of 'יְהֵא חֶלְקִי' wishes points to practices worth striving for: שלש סעודות, daily פסוקי דזמרא, davening at sunrise and sunset, extending שבת, bringing people to learn, careful צדקה, and bearing false suspicion.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
They suspected me, and there was nothing in me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a personal example of step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא testifies that he was falsely suspected, so he shares in the portion רבי יוסי described.

steps.title: Five relations, five great sons
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says he had relations five times and fathered five sons who became great scholars, and the sons are listed by name.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: I had relations five times, and I planted five cedars in ישראל. Who are they? רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי, רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי, רבי חלפתא son of רבי יוסי, רבי אבטילס son of רבי יוסי, and רבי מנחם son of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: This is another personal statement from רבי יוסי, continuing the list from the earlier steps. He compares his five sons to tall, strong cedar trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Cedars' is a picture of great Torah scholars who stand tall in ישראל. The list of five names explains who the 'cedars' are. As written, the statement suggests he had relations only five times, which the גמרא will question soon.

keyTerms.meaning: Cedar trees, here a picture of great scholars

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
I engaged in relations five times,
and I planted five cedars in Israel.
And who are they?
Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei,
and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei,
and Rabbi Chalafta son of Rabbi Yosei,
and Rabbi Avtilas son of Rabbi Yosei,
and Rabbi Menachem son of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: חָמֵשׁ בְּעִילוֹת בָּעַלְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of רבי יוסי's personal statements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי fathered five sons who became great Torah scholars.

steps.title: What about the son named ורדימס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the count of five by pointing to another son, ורדימס.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also ורדימס!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that רבי יוסי had another son, ורדימס, so it seems there were six sons, not five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list named only five sons, but ורדימס is known as a son of רבי יוסי too. That seems to break the count of 'five cedars.'

keyTerms.meaning: ורדימס, a name the גמרא first takes to be another son of רבי יוסי

phrases.english: But there is Vardimas!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the list of five sons.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of exactly five sons
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known sixth son, ורדימס, seems to make the count six.

steps.title: ורדימס is מנחם's nickname
steps.stepSummary: ורדימס and מנחם are the same person. He was called ורדימס because his face looked like a rose.
steps.simpleTranslation: ורדימס is מנחם. Why was he called ורדימס? Because his face was like a rose (ורד).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ורדימס is not a sixth son. It is a nickname for מנחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name ורדימס comes from the word ורד, a rose, because מנחם's face was beautiful like a rose. So the count of five sons stays correct.

keyTerms.meaning: And why did they call him...?

phrases.english: Vardimas is the same as Menachem,
and why did they call him "Vardimas"?
Because his face was like a rose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about ורדימס.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identification: two names refer to one person
steps.terutzMaskana: ורדימס is a nickname for מנחם, so there are still five sons.

steps.title: Did רבי יוסי fail to keep the מצוה of עונה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording: if he had relations only five times, he did not keep the מצוה of עונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבי יוסי did not keep the מצוה of עונה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the plain meaning of 'I had relations five times.' Read literally, it means a great צדיק neglected a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband has a Torah duty of עונה, which means being with his wife regularly. Having relations only five times in a whole marriage would break that duty. That cannot be true of רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband's duty of regular marital relations with his wife

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Yosei
did not fulfill the מצוה of onah?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מִצְוַת עוֹנָה לֹא קִיֵּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the opening words of step 28 and challenges their plain meaning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read literally, they mean רבי יוסי failed to keep מצות עונה, which is impossible for him.

steps.title: Rereading: five times, each time done twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the statement as 'I had relations five times and did so again,' meaning five times he acted in a way that led to a son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: I had relations five times and did it again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of רבי יוסי's words. He was not counting every time he was with his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ושניתי means 'and I repeated it.' One explanation is that the חכמים taught that doing it again helps bring male children. So the 'five' refers only to the five times that produced his sons, not to his whole married life.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'five' in רבי יוסי's statement counts the five times that led to his five great sons. It does not mean he neglected מצות עונה.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
I engaged in relations five times and I did so again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: חָמֵשׁ בְּעִילוֹת בָּעַלְתִּי וְשָׁנִיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the עונה challenge by rereading the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי was with his wife only five times in total.
steps.terutzMaskana: The five times are the ones that led to sons, done twice each time. They are not his total.

steps.title: He called his wife 'my home' and his ox 'my field'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי never said 'my wife' or 'my ox.' He called his wife 'my home' and his ox 'my field.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: In all my days I never called my wife 'my wife' or my ox 'my ox.' Instead I called my wife 'my home' and my ox 'my field.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another personal statement from רבי יוסי, this time about how he spoke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He used names that show what each one means to him. His wife is the heart of the home, and the ox is the main worker in the field. This shows refined speech and respect.

keyTerms.meaning: In all my days, never in my life

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
In all my days I did not call my wife "my wife"
nor my ox "my ox";
rather, my wife I called "my home,"
and my ox, "my field."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מִיָּמַי לֹא קָרִיתִי לְאִשְׁתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New statement in the series of רבי יוסי's personal statements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי called his wife 'my home' and his ox 'my field.'

steps.title: He never looked at his circumcision
steps.stepSummary: Out of modesty, רבי יוסי never looked at his own מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: In all my days I never looked at my circumcision.
steps.whatsHappening: Another statement from רבי יוסי, this one about his extreme modesty. It sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows a very high level of personal modesty (צניעות). The גמרא will compare it to a well-known statement of רבי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
In all my days I never looked at my circumcision.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מִיָּמַי לֹא נִסְתַּכַּלְתִּי בַּמִּילָּה שֶׁלִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New statement in the series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי never looked at his own מילה.

steps.title: רבי was called holy for this same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי said he was called 'our holy רבי' for this exact practice, so why wasn't רבי יוסי called holy too?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But they asked רבי: Why are you called 'רבינו הקדוש'? He told them: In all my days I never looked at my circumcision.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 34. רבי gave this practice as the special reason he was called 'holy.' If רבי יוסי did the same thing, it seems he should have had that title too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not that רבי יוסי's practice is impossible. The question is: if this practice earned רבי the title רבינו הקדוש, why didn't רבי יוסי get the same title? The question is not spelled out, but it is the point of the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our holy רבי,' the title of רבי יהודה הנשיא

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה. It is not רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't they say to Rebbi:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא קָרוּ לָךְ רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ?
phrases.english: Why do they call you "our holy Rebbi"?
He said to them:
In all my days I never looked at my circumcision.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 34 using רבי's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If this practice was the special reason רבי was called holy, רבי יוסי should have been called holy too.

steps.title: רבי had an extra level of modesty
steps.stepSummary: רבי had another, extra practice: he never put his hand below his belt.
steps.simpleTranslation: In רבי there was another quality: he never put his hand beneath his belt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי had an additional level of modesty that רבי יוסי did not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of them never looked at their מילה. But רבי also never put his hand below his belt. That extra step is what earned him the title 'holy.'

phrases.english: In Rebbi there was another matter,
that he did not put his hand beneath his belt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from רבי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: רבי had an extra practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both had the same modesty, so both should have been called holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי had an extra practice of not putting his hand below his belt, which earned him the title.

steps.title: His walls never saw the seams of his robe
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי was so modest that the walls of his house never saw the seams of his robe.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי said: In all my days the walls of my house never saw the seams of my robe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another statement from רבי יוסי about his modesty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One explanation is that he got undressed only under his blanket. So even when alone, he never exposed the inner side of his clothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The beams or walls of my house
The seams or edges of my robe

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei said:
In all my days the walls of my house did not see
the seams of my robe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מִיָּמַי לֹא רָאוּ קוֹרוֹת בֵּיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the list of רבי יוסי's statements after the side discussion about רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי kept himself covered even when alone in his house.

steps.title: He never went against his colleagues' words
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי always listened to his colleagues. Even though he was not a כהן, if they told him to go up to the דוכן, he would go up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי said: In all my days I never went against what my colleagues said. I know I am not a כהן, but if my colleagues tell me, 'Go up to the דוכן,' I go up.
steps.whatsHappening: Another statement from רבי יוסי, this time about how much he respected his colleagues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דוכן is the platform where כהנים stand to give ברכת כהנים. Saying he would go up even though he is not a כהן shows how far he would go to listen to his friends. Commentators discuss how this could be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The platform from which the כהנים bless the people

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּמַי לֹא עָבַרְתִּי עַל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵרַי.
phrases.english: In all my days I never went against the words of my colleagues.
I know about myself that I am not a priest,
yet if my colleagues say to me:
"Go up to the platform," I go up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מִיָּמַי לֹא עָבַרְתִּי עַל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵרַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series with a new character trait.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי always did what his colleagues told him.

steps.title: He never took back his words
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי never said something and then denied it later.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי said: In all my days I never said something and then went back on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The last statement here. It shows that רבי יוסי stood behind his words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some explain that when he said something about a person, good or bad, he never later denied saying it. His words were completely reliable.

keyTerms.meaning: And I went back on it, retracted

steps.whatToRemember: These statements together paint רבי יוסי as a model of modesty, refined speech, respect for colleagues, and honesty.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei said:
In all my days I never said something
and then went back on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מִיָּמַי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי דָּבָר וְחָזַרְתִּי לַאֲחוֹרַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series with another character trait.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי never went back on anything he said.

steps.title: רב נחמן: three meals on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says he deserves reward because he kept the מצוה of שלש סעודות on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: May I be rewarded, because I kept the מצוה of three meals on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps listing sages' special practices. רב נחמן names his: eating three meals on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of the earlier steps about רבי יוסי's good habits. The phrase "תיתי לי" opens a new series of short personal statements. Each one names one מצוה the speaker was especially careful with.

keyTerms.meaning: "May it come to me": may I receive reward
The three meals eaten on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: "תיתי לי" is not bragging. It is a request that the merit of the מצוה should stand for the speaker.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: May I be rewarded,
because I kept the three meals on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sages' personal practices that began with רבי יוסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן took pride in carefully keeping שלש סעודות on שבת.

steps.title: רב יהודה: concentration in prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says he deserves reward for praying with real focus.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: May I be rewarded, because I kept the practice of concentrating during prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: Another sage adds his special practice. רב יהודה names focused, thoughtful prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "עיון תפלה" means paying close attention to what you are saying when you daven. This is a mental, inner practice, not a physical action.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: May I be rewarded,
because I kept concentration in prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the same list of statements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה was especially careful to concentrate when he prayed.

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: never walking bareheaded
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע never walked four אמות with his head uncovered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: May I be rewarded, because I never walked four אמות with my head uncovered.
steps.whatsHappening: Another sage names his practice. He always kept his head covered, even for a short walk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four אמות is a very short distance, about 2 meters. Even for that, he never went bareheaded. Covering the head shows awareness of יראת שמים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
May I be rewarded, because I never walked
four cubits with my head uncovered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: תֵּיתֵי לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע never walked even four אמות bareheaded.

steps.title: רב ששת: the מצוה of תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says he deserves reward for carefully keeping the מצוה of תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: May I be rewarded, because I kept the מצוה of תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת names תפילין as the מצוה he was most careful with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that רב ששת kept this מצוה with special care. It is not simply that he performed it.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: May I be rewarded,
because I kept the מצוה of tefillin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת was especially careful with תפילין.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the מצוה of ציצית
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן adds a second practice: carefully keeping ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: May I be rewarded, because I kept the מצוה of ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן appears again with a second practice, ציצית. This leads into the next discussion, which is about ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "וְאָמַר" ("and he said") shows this is a second statement from the same רב נחמן as in step 40. Mentioning ציצית sets up the story about רבה and his ציצית.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same רב נחמן from step 40. He has two "תיתי לי" statements.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said: May I be rewarded,
because I kept the מצוה of tzitzit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement from רב נחמן, which leads into the topic of ציצית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן was especially careful with ציצית.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks what רבה was most careful about
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks רב יוסף בריה דרבה which מצוה his father רבה was most careful with.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to רב יוסף בריה דרבה: Your father, what was he most careful about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new question. It asks which מצוה רבה was most careful with, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question asking for information, not a challenge. It continues the theme of special practices. This time the practice is learned from a son about his father.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two people named רב יוסף here. The first is the asker. The second is the son of רבה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him,
to Rav Yosef son of Rabba:
Your father, in what was he most careful?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from sages describing themselves to asking about another sage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מצוה רבה kept with the most care.

steps.title: The answer: ציצית
steps.stepSummary: The son answers that רבה was most careful with ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: The son answers the question. His father's special מצוה was ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This one-word answer connects back to רב נחמן's ציצית statement in step 44. It also sets up the story that follows, which shows this care in action.

phrases.english: He said to him: In tzitzit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 45.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבה was most careful with ציצית.

steps.title: Story: רבה on the stairs with a torn string
steps.stepSummary: A string of רבה's ציצית tore while he was climbing stairs. He did not continue until he attached a new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day he was going up the stairs. A string of his ציצית tore, and he did not come down or move on until he put a new string on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to show how careful רבה was with ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not say the garment had become unfit. The point is רבה's zeal: once his ציצית were no longer complete, he would not move on, up or down, until he had attached a new string.

keyTerms.meaning: He placed it (attached a new string)

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד הֲוָה קָא סָלֵיק בְּדַרְגָּא.
phrases.english: One day he was going up the stairs.
A string tore on him,
and he did not come down or move on,
until he had placed a new one on.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד הֲוָה קָא סָלֵיק בְּדַרְגָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that illustrates the answer in step 46.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a string of רבה's ציצית tore, he did not move on until he had attached a new one.
steps.whatToRemember: These sages each picked one מצוה to keep with extra care. רבה's ציצית story shows what that care looked like in real life.

steps.title: אביי begins: when a young scholar finishes a tractate
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins his own "תיתי לי" statement about a young תלמיד חכם who finishes a מסכת. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: May I be rewarded, because when I see a young תלמיד חכם who has finished his מסכת...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a new statement about his own special practice. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This returns to the "תיתי לי" pattern from steps 40–44. אביי's practice is tied to Torah learning: what he does when a young scholar finishes a מסכת. What he actually does is explained next.
steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished. Wait for the next passage to learn what אביי did.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: May I be rewarded,
because when I see a young Torah scholar
who has completed his tractate

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the list of "תיתי לי" statements after the story about רבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's special practice concerns honoring a young scholar who completes a מסכת (details on the next amud).
